title: DuckDB does not properly read TIMETZ types
body:
### What happens?

The attached parquet file as a single TIMETZ column and DuckDB can not properly parse the timezone value. 
The parquet file viewed via https://dataconverter.io/view/parquet looks like this:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/735cf489-4da8-4340-bfcf-1b9121501d17)

However, DuckDB returns the following:
```
D select * from 'timetz_column.parquet';
┌─────────────────────┐
│        col33        │
│ time with time zone │
├─────────────────────┤
│ at:33:32.627776+00  │
│ iv:26:11.627776+00  │
│ IL:29:15.627776+00  │
└─────────────────────┘
```
[timetz_column.parquet.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17651418/timetz_column.parquet.zip)

### To Reproduce

Download the attached parquet file. With DuckDB cli, run the following:
```
duckdb
D select * from 'timetz_column.parquet';
```

### OS:

MacOS M1 

### DuckDB Version:

1.1.3 (and older versions)

### DuckDB Client:

CLI

### Hardware:

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
> Is `TIMESTAMPTZ` also affected?

@participant1 there is no time zone embedded in parquet timestamps (or in SQL `TIMESTAMPTZ` types), and this path is well tested, so the answer here is almost certainly no.
 
`TIMETZ` is another matter, and I have been unable to find any documentation on how `isAdjustedToUTC` affects `TIME` types. The data in the file provided is outside the range of valid time values `[00:00:00-24:00:00]`:

```
301:33:32.627776    &raw_micros	const int64_t	1085612627776
290:26:11.627776    &raw_micros	const int64_t	1045571627776
294:29:15.627776    &raw_micros	const int64_t	1060155627776
```
In debug, the code throws because the hour is out of range, so I suspect the garbage display is caused by the formatter assuming that the data was validated on input. Unfortunately, it appears that the parquet reader is not validating the input properly. 

Right now it assumes that the time is a count of µs since the epoch and set the offset to 0, but that may not be correct. I can probably fix this @reporter if you can tell me how the file was created or point me at how parquet represents the offsets?

I did notice that the hours are correct if they are taken mod 24, and the div is 12 for all three values, so it looks like the times have been offset by 12 hours. I have never seen this representation before, it does not appear to be documented anywhere and I am loath to assume that offsets are encoded in this way (minutes?, seconds? negative hours west of Greenwich?)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Great findings @participant3, thanks for looking at this! 

I extracted col33 from a larger dataset using using DuckDB cli to create the `timetz_column.parquet`. This may have had some affect on the data. For reference, the initial dataset starts out in a postgres DB which I used two different SQL tools to query col33 (Apache Drill and PSQL):

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/65f193ca-04cc-457c-82a5-b506e41e30f9)

The pqsl output on the right shows the timezones but they are technically not valid. The left (apache output) seems to be adjusted based on the offsets. I used ApacheDrill to output this data to a parquet file: [timetz_column_generate_by_apache_drill.parquet.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17670792/timetz_column_generate_by_apache_drill.parquet.zip)

This file CAN be parsed by duckdb:
```
D select * from '~/Downloads/timetz_column_generate_by_apache_drill.parquet';
┌─────────────────────┐
│        col33        │
│ time with time zone │
├─────────────────────┤
│ 15:08:21+00         │
│ 04:01:00+00         │
│ 08:04:04+00         │
└─────────────────────┘
```
Internally, we query from postgres and use `ParquetWriter` from https://github.com/apache/parquet-java to produce the parquet file that DuckDB fails to read which is also apache. After the data gets through our system the `part-0.parquet` file is produced:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/264962fe-9f85-44a2-9b4e-2d015cdf7203)

As you can see, the `timetz_column.parquet` file is certainly corrupted because `13:33:32.6227` doesn't look anything like the initial dataset. Apache Drill _can_ parse the `part-0.parquet` and these time values are adjusted to GMT which matches how other parts of our system display this data. Ultimately this is what we expected from DuckDB as well.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
I'm confused by this:

> The pqsl output on the right shows the timezones but they are technically not valid.

Why are they not valid? PG supports `TIMETZ` values with offsets ±15:59:59 (the docs leave off the seconds, but I have verified this empirically). It looks more to me like the values in the PG test table were not inserted correctly?

Incidentally, the `TIME WITH TIME ZONE` type has an even worse name than  `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE`: it doesn't model time zones at all (how could it without a date?) it just stores an offset and then has some rather confusing comparison semantics bolted on top of that.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Thanks, some things are becoming clearer. So the original data has the fractional offsets and this path works:

PG => PG extension => duckdb => CLI output

I'm still not clear how `part-0.parquet` is produced? Above you say

> After the data gets through our system the `part-0.parquet` file is produced:

so it sounds like some other tool is producing this parquet file? You also say

> Viewing the `part-0.parquet` (which was generated by Java code with Apache API) with the online parquet viewer, I see the following:

which suggests that your system is using a Java tool of some kind to produce this file?  If this is the case, then I think the problem is in that tool. 

I'm also not clear what is meant by 

> This seems to be correctly adjusted to GMT but duckdb still can't read it

No adjusting to GMT is done with `TTZ` types except for sorting. I can see that e.g., `10:07:21+13:59` is equivalent to `20:08:21` (if you wrap) but that is not the same data type (Is it `TIME`?) and the two values are not the same in the SQL definition.

Unless I have misunderstood something, it sounds to me like the Java tool does not handle this type correctly (or at least for SQL). It certainly sounds like something outside of DuckDB is producing corrupt `TIME` columns with the `isAdjustedToUTC` flag set. So for us, there are two issues:

- If there is a path to producing a corrupt parquet column using _only_ DuckDB, then that is a bug. (Note that you can insert into a table using the values as strings and bypass the PG connector)
- If it is possible for outside tools to create corrupt columns of this type, then we should probably either wrap them or throw an error.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I have new insights. Our java code parses postgres data and generates the parquet sets `isAdjustedToUTC` as true by default and these third-party libraries: 
* "org.apache.parquet:parquet-avro:1.14.1",
* "org.apache.parquet:parquet-hadoop:1.14.1"

The `TIME_WITH_TIMEZONE` value of col33 in postgres (`10:07:21+13:59`) gets extracted and converted to `-13899000` milliseconds since midnight. Here's that calculation: 
* Local time in milliseconds: `10 * 3600 * 1000 + 7 * 60 * 1000 + 21 * 1000 = 36441000` milliseconds
* Time zone offset: `+13:59` (which is `13 * 3600 + 59 * 60 = 50340` seconds or `50340000` milliseconds)
* Adjusted milliseconds: `36441000 - 50340000 = -13899000` milliseconds

@participant3 Does that seem valid? Can DuckDB handle negative timetz values?

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: The math makes sense I suppose, but the information for the offset has been lost so there is not a lot we can do with it. Basically, we could produce a time+offset starting with 00:00:00+13899000ms but there are a large number of legal possibilities. We should throw, though, as the values are not valid SQL `TIMETZ` values.

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: I think what we could do here is wrap all values to [00:00:00, 24:00:00).

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I agree in a sense but perhaps this check should also be done elsewhere (outside of DuckDB), such as before it's been written to parquet. From what I found today, I think there _is_ an expectation that the data being written to parquet should be non-negative given that this type _should_ represent a "time-of-day" value. However I couldn't find any documentation supporting this other than AI answers. In our case this could be an issue better suited for: https://github.com/apache/parquet-java. At the moment, my team might consider invalidating this data on the Java side, before it becomes a parquet. Thanks for the info and efforts getting to this point! @participant3
